places.name: Cabin stream
places.note: Stream edge near cabin; possible site for a wheat patch.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Porch crafting table
places.note: Crafting table; currently hard to reach through cobblestone/plank obstruction.
places.author: Gary

places.name: My first wheat seed
places.note: Wheat planted on the stream-side shared row; block is the crop space at y=115.
places.author: Margo

places.name: North cabin crafting table
places.note: Working table; use from the ledge. Shared with Margo.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Margo stream wheat seedling
places.note: My first verified wheat planting: farmland at 100,115,-198 beside the open stream bank.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Margo stream-bank worktable
places.note: My crafting table on the clear grassy bank, a short walk from the new wheat crop.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Margo accidental dirt shaft
places.note: Accidental Baritone excavation; dead-end dirt/stone hole with zombie risk. Not a route down.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West stream bank clay scout
places.note: Northwest edge checked with Margo: visible bank is grass and dirt; no exposed clay seen.
places.author: Gary

places.name: North-coast breathing test
places.note: Dry ridge reached after submerged crossing; surface rescue paused and resumed travel.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Birch meadow rest bench
places.note: Small birch-slab seat on the open west slope below the flower meadow; crafting table is nearby uphill at (142,109,-180).
places.author: Gary

places.name: East stream workbench
places.note: Working crafting table east of the wheat patch, at the foot of the cabin slope.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East extension of stream wheat patch
places.note: Five new wheat along the east edge of Gary's stream wheat patch, distinct from Margo's plot.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Eastern grass seed meadow
places.note: Short grass drops wheat and hemp seeds. Stop mining once enough seeds are in your bag.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East birch chicken clearing
places.note: One free-range chicken was wandering here. Route around the old builds and pits in the woods.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Stream composter
places.note: Beside the stream workbench. Add surplus plant matter for bone meal. Margo set it against the hillside.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Cabin stream stairs
places.note: Foot of four cobblestone steps north to Gary's cabin door. Use these dry steps and stay out of the wheat rows.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Stream wheat patch
places.note: Gary's signed east-bank field. 24 wheat, plus hemp and flax. Right-click mature wheat to harvest and replant.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Northwest sheep ridge
places.note: White sheep last seen here by mossy boulders, roaming west. A cow was a dozen blocks farther northwest.
places.author: Gary

places.name: South rim farm crossing east approach
places.note: Dry route between the stream workbench and the west-side birch grove. Keep along the southern rim of the planted plots.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Sheep by south crossing slope
places.note: The sheared white sheep last slipped past the south gate. Check the open grass south and east of the pen.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Gary's cabin
places.note: Lit cabin with working oak door, reserve seed chest and shared white bed. Use the bed to set respawn. Approach from the Cabin stream stairs.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shared cabin bed
places.note: White bed Gary made and offered for shared use, inside the lit cabin.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West cabin furnace
places.note: Shared working furnace on the west hillside, lit by a torch. It smelted iron and made charcoal. Stand on the level terrace block just east.
places.author: Gary

places.name: South rim farm crossing west approach
places.note: Birch sign directs east to the cabined farm by the dry south rim. The pen lies just north of here.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Sand on west ridge
places.note: Nearby sand blocks detected below the birch crest, high above the coast. Check footing before digging.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West ridge sand bank
places.note: Larger deposit with at least fifteen sand blocks detected on the west ridge. Start from the grassy crest and watch the south-facing drop.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West coast bucket descent
places.note: Reached the sea here by following the bare stone slope south. Filled a bucket at the shoreline and climbed back with no injury. Steep slope, take care on foot.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East wheat watering slab
places.note: Water-filled birch half-slab fed from the west coast. It waters the east crop rows and is shallow at the stair approach.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Chicken in west bank pen
places.note: Verified one adult chicken behind the closed north gate. The entrance has a middle divider and is approachable along the outside east fence.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East birch waystone
places.note: Activated Waystone Lukmicred by right-click. Approach from open birches on the south, staying clear of the pits to the west.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Second east chicken sighting
places.note: Live adult chicken found east of Lukmicred waystone. A return route south around the waystone uses the open birch ledges.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West bank chicken flock
places.note: Margo and Gary bred two adult chickens and verified a third chicken, the chick, inside. Keep both outer gates shut. Use the middle divider to enter or exit.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West bank livestock pen
places.note: Shared flock of two adults and one chick in the lit south compartment. Both outer gates and the divider were shut after breeding. Open one gate at a time and keep breeding adults for eggs.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West bank worktable
places.note: Crafting table just north of the chicken pen. Approach from the north on the open terrace.
places.author: Margo

places.name: North ridge coal approach
places.note: Surface lip of the shallow coal cut. Approach from the south. Follow the stepped cut and torch; keep to the rim when passing.
places.author: Margo

places.name: South ravine clay band
places.note: Dry torch-lit tunnel reaches the seam from the east. I collected 24 clay balls with a stone shovel and there is more below and along the sides.
places.author: Gary

places.name: South ravine clay tunnel approach
places.note: Torch marks westward descent to the clay; dry both ways. A zombie approached out of shade near the surface exit, so have a weapon ready.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Gary's cabin chest
places.note: Shared with Margo. Northwest corner of the cabin. Seed reserves, eggs, shears, clay for a Coke Oven, and starter engineering supplies.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West ridge workable sand shelf
places.note: Open natural sand shelf reached from the north via the grassy crest. A short bounded mine collected sand here with a shovel.
places.author: Margo

places.name: South coal deposit reported by spesk01
places.note: spesk01 reports a large coal deposit. I have not verified surface access.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West bank worktable furnace
places.note: Shared furnace beside the west-bank table, just north of the chicken pen. Bring fuel and check for an active batch.
places.author: Margo

places.name: East workshop bench and chest
places.note: Indoor-free workshop storage sits one step below the southwest crafting bench. Use it for the oven's products and workshop supplies.
places.author: Margo

places.name: East oven standing spot
places.note: One block east of the Coke Oven front. Look west at the middle-layer face. Approach from the south field via the birch sign and stay clear of crops.
places.author: Margo

places.name: East workshop Coke Oven
places.note: Working shared oven. Open from the east face via the field approach. Two coal made two coke and one creosote bucket. Workbench and chest near the south edge.
places.author: Margo

places.name: South ravine copper and osmium approach
places.note: Proven dry entrance to a lit short ore cut. Use the shallow ore torch as the first waypoint and this marker to climb back out.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Birch meadow stone exposure
places.note: Open natural stone and gravel east of the flower-slope bench, with visible ore. Gather from surface exposures and leave a walkable rim.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East workshop approach
places.note: Lit bend between the south edge of the wheat and the workshop steps. Go east to the bench, then turn north around the oven to its east face.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East workshop terrace
places.note: Lit 5x5 cobblestone terrace. Stand on the east side to open the Coke Oven. From the East workshop approach take the south-edge step and turn north around the oven.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East workshop Mekanism access
places.note: Stand here just north of the oven's east hatch. Look west into the infuser or aim over its top to use the Heat Generator behind it.
places.author: Margo

places.name: South ravine shallow ore torch
places.note: First landing and torch inside the dry shallow cut. From the surface approach go one west, two down and five north; use surface approach to exit.
places.author: Margo

places.name: South ravine osmium landing
places.note: Lit eastern stair ends here. A stone pick works. Osmium remains at floor height beside the landing. Return via the bend to the shallow cut and surface approach.
places.author: Gary

places.name: South ravine osmium stair bend
places.note: At the lower end of the eastward stair, turn north for the osmium landing. Up west to the shallow ore torch and surface.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East workshop chest standing spot
places.note: Stand on the west side of the chest to open it without the bench or birch trunk blocking your view. Approach from the field path.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East workshop ravine junction
places.note: Follow path and gravel east toward Birch flower meadow. Up west is the workshop stair and stream. The signed bend stays below the oven.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Southeast gold stair working face
places.note: One natural raw gold block recovered. More natural gold lies nearby; the return uses the lit crosscut above.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Birch meadow ravine turn
places.note: Leave the flower meadow toward the birch rest bench on the lower southeastern slope. Reverse northwest on the path for the East workshop.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Southeast shore gold stair
places.note: Lit hand-cut shore entrance. From both marked bends, follow the torched passage across the level water bypass to the gold face.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore return skeleton pocket
places.note: Several skeletons and a creeper in this low pocket; approach from above in daylight.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Gold shore east bypass ridge
places.note: Use the open slope farther east to bypass the skeleton pocket and trapping stone shaft.
places.author: Margo

places.name: South ravine upper trail
places.note: Above the shallow ore entrance. Follow the downhill path on the east side to the lip, then turn west into the approach. From the mouth, the passage runs north to Margo's shallow ore torch.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West bank materials chest
places.note: Shared bulk materials beside west-bank furnace and table. The six osmium and two iron ingots are reserved for wind.
places.author: Margo

places.name: East workshop furnace
places.note: Shared furnace immediately west of the crafting bench. Use from the chest's west standing spot. Check active input and output before loading.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Stream rail landing
places.note: Stand here from the east wheat path to approach spesk01's powered line. He offered normal use and set out carts.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Northwest birch pigs
places.note: Two pigs wandered either side of this clearing. I saw them live during a scout, with no attempt to lead them.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Northwest birch cow
places.note: One adult cow was repeatedly seen on the grassy north slope here.
places.author: Gary

places.name: North ridge pig sighting
places.note: A lone pig roamed on this higher grassy shelf just north of the ruins.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East workshop wind tower
places.note: Wind Generator at Y120 with five cables down its south side. Metallurgic Infuser accessible from east beside Coke Oven.
places.author: Margo

places.name: East workshop infuser aisle
places.note: Clear standing spot at the east end of the aisle. Look west at the Metallurgic Infuser beside the oven; I opened it and saw two alloys from Margo's first wind batch.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Far northwest sheep grove
places.note: Two adult sheep seen on adjacent wooded slopes. The northwestern one was five blocks lower at the first sighting.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East workshop ore processor
places.note: Stand in the east aisle. Enrichment Chamber is north and the Metallurgic Infuser is west. Both are on the same wind line.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Southeast coast sheep
places.note: One adult sheep seen down the birch slope near the coast. The ridge just north gives dry access.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Southeast lava pocket survey
places.note: Lava sensed from the east slope. Broad patch at this level. Access and source blocks unverified. Margo has a nearby route via her old gold stair.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore lava branch turn
places.note: At Y52 leave the gold stair west for five blocks, then turn north on the lit level branch. Preserve the old stair southeast of the turn.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore lava bucket landing
places.note: From the Y52 branch turn walk north to the widened alcove. Stand on its eastmost stone by the low opening and aim down through it. Got a full bucket without stepping off the floor.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Meadow bunkhouse
places.note: Stone-and-birch bunk just north of the meadow path. Lit refuge with door, workbench and chest. The bed is Margo's active respawn.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore lava branch junction
places.note: On the lit gold stair, turn west here before the lower bend. Follow the level branch to the sign and turn north for the lava draw bay.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore water bucket shelf
places.note: Dry grass above the coast. Filled two buckets by aiming down southwest past the grass into open sea. Approach from gold stair mouth via higher grass, no need to enter water.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore lava north ports
places.note: Walk east of the draw lips until the north bend, then west on the dry level rock to this torch and low cobble cap. Aim low under the cap or down through the south slit to reach more lava.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore overland ridge
places.note: Daylight high-ground route between workshop meadow and the shore gold stair. Pass east of the low sheltering-mob pocket. Ridge drops are still rough.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore portal approach
places.note: Lit portal east of the dry lava branch. From the gold stair turn toward the draw bay, then take the torch-marked side room. Use the protected entry.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore west terrace bypass
places.note: Walk west of the gold stair on natural grass as far as this rise. The wheat terraces directly west belong to spesk01, so turn north here for the ravine route.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore dry ravine climb
places.note: Dry ground between the west shore turn and South ravine upper trail. From the shore zig north-east onto the green saddle, then north-west up the ravine side. I walked uphill with no damage.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore portal corridor entrance
places.note: Lit at the east opening on the lava branch. Nether return sent Margo to the jungle rail claim. She opened the west birch doors and reached the southwest paved step. Leave the other portal and claim intact.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Northwest ridge second cow
places.note: Saw a lone adult outside the old sheep grove on the walk up from home. Bring wheat and use short ridge waypoints for a future pair.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Northwest stone bench coal
places.note: Natural flat stone bench past the old sheep grove. Several coal blocks are reachable from above. Four collected from shallow cuts, more visible. Keep to the solid rim.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Northwest stone shelf escape stair
places.note: Lit narrow stair built up from a dark slate pocket after a 3-heart fall. A torch marks the little turn by a hollow birch log. Keep surface travel off the gully west of the coal bench.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Stream fishing bend
places.note: Stand on the dry south rim beside the stream and cast north-northwest along the water. I used yaw 166 and pitch 24. Reel quickly when the red float sinks out of sight.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore diamond stair branch
places.note: Lit natural-stone staircase east and then south from the gold access. Tested climb back to the shore junction.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Birch meadow cook fire
places.note: Raised campfire one step south from South ravine footpath on grass. Stand on the west side. From the marked grass face southeast and aim at the wooden side of the hearth to cook. Stay on the grass while picking up food.
places.author: Gary

places.name: South stone face pillager ledge
places.note: Two pillagers visible across the stone face NW in daylight. Steep ocean drop. Stay on the plateau north of the lip; avoid the ledge.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West inland sheep pair
places.note: Two wild sheep on high birch ground above the southwest coast. Dry approach from east and north.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Far northwest mixed herds
places.note: Wild cows, sheep and pigs at the birch edge southeast of the large exposed stone plateau.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore obsidian casting tray
places.note: Dry east alcove across from lava ledge. Pour one lava onto the lower stone by the water, then mine from the walkway with diamond. Twelve pieces collected unhurt.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore far lava draw step
places.note: Use the dry narrow cobble approach and one natural lower tread only. Aim down from here, with lava at Y50 off both sides. Several real sources remain farther west.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Far northwest berry thicket
places.note: Harvested eight wild sweet berries. Daylit eastern ridge reaches upper torch, mushroom shelf wall torch, then ground torches. Skeletons killed me on first unlit approach. Bushes are beside the lower torch.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Northwest berry ridge approach
places.note: Approach from east with short hops toward upper grass torch, then stay on the lit east side of the dark oak edge. Walk downhill one step at a time.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore quartz portal vestibule
places.note: Stand in the sealed-side room just west of the frame. The marked Nether partner sits on a warped terrace.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Warped terrace shore portal
places.note: Verified partner of the Shore quartz portal vestibule. Use the west landing. The east terrace rim overlooks a large drop.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Cabin berry strip
places.note: Four shared sweet berry bushes on the sunny shelf east of the cabin. Approach from the north side of the row. Use a tool or empty hand to pick from beside the bush.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Warped terrace portal door
places.note: Torch and sign on west side. A single step leads up to the birch door. Approach from the west, away from the east drop.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Warped north quartz cut
places.note: Follow torches on the natural ridge north from the portal. Cobble step at the mouth of a shallow cut into the quartz seam.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Warped quartz working pocket
places.note: A shallow bore from the ridge cut. I took 26 quartz and left ore under the walking floor. Take the torch line back south to the door.
places.author: Margo

places.name: South birch wild bee nest
places.note: Wild nest above the meadow. Honey at 5 of 5 with one bee inside when checked. Approach uphill from the ravine footpath.
places.author: Gary

places.name: South birch nest ledge
places.note: Dry standing spot north of the first wild nest, with a clear view of its underside.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore supply alcove
places.note: Bench and chest recessed into stone just outside the portal vestibule. Quartz and supplies can be staged here above the dry branch.
places.author: Margo

places.name: South hill sand pocket
places.note: Natural sand in the open hill west of the railway. Took three surface blocks for bottles.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East stream furnace
places.note: Second shared furnace tucked behind the workbench. Opens from the workbench's usual south standing spot.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Warped glowstone landing
places.note: Cobblestone floor and rail under netherrack roof. Mine face from behind the endstop. Keep the glowstone floor intact under the endstop.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Warped glowstone bore bridge
places.note: Approach from warped forest west side, climb to the narrow railed cobble bridge, go east into the bore. Inside, descend at the far end to the glowstone landing.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Warped glowstone bridge approach
places.note: Torch at former warped stem on straight approach from the west. Up the one-block cobblestone step to the railed span; stay between rails.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Warped quartz-glowstone fork
places.note: Torch beyond quartz cut. Glowstone loop goes east past the trees to the signed bridge; follow lights. Return west to the quartz cut, then south on the portal trail.
places.author: Margo

places.name: North ridge zombie hollow rim
places.note: Shallow hole beside the mossy boulder. A zombie caught me at the rim and again on the south approach. Use the level west shelf and keep clear of the opening.
places.author: Gary

places.name: North ridge iron stair
places.note: Lit stair cut into the west ridge, heading north. Approach from the west and keep away from the zombie hollow to the east.
places.author: Gary

places.name: North ridge iron wall branch
places.note: From Gary’s signed North ridge iron stair descend straight north. Keep the cobblestone landing step and mine the sides. I added a torch in the branch; rich ore remains.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Southeast kelp shore step
places.note: Open grass above natural shore. Swim west from here for the shallow tall kelp. Keep clear of the terrace and overhanging works to the northwest.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West pasture workbench
places.note: Crafting table beside the southern grass shelf of the cattle and sheep pasture.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Southeast shallow kelp
places.note: Swim out from Southeast kelp shore step; trim the underwater tops and pick up floating kelp at the surface. Leave the roots.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West bank grass pasture
places.note: Use the south gate by the cobble steps and outside crafting table. Two gates flank a three-block-wide entry; close each before opening the next. The east pair is backup.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Cabin work chest
places.note: Shared spare tools, wool, seeds and building materials beside the new interior workbench. Pantry is the neighboring chest at the back.
places.author: Gary

places.name: North ridge shallow coal room
places.note: Lit passage from the North ridge coal approach through the zinc landing. Follow south shelf around the one-block drop. Natural coal blocks and ordinary ore remain.
places.author: Margo

places.name: North birch hay cache
places.note: A generated Lootr chest in a lantern-lit hay pile. My copy contained six starter potatoes. Approach on the western ridge.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Stream potato row
places.note: Four potato starts in the lit east-bank field. Replant this row before you take spare potatoes.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Near northwest pig shelf
places.note: Saw wild pig #48273 on the grassy slope. It wandered southeast to the lower birch shelf.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Southeast tall kelp shoal
places.note: Cut the upper stalk while floating and pause directly above for the drops. Leave the roots. Approach from Southeast kelp shore step via the shallow kelp marker.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Cabin to pig pen west steps
places.note: From the cabin porch step west, then follow the two stone steps out of the shallow dip and the path northwest to the pig pen.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Northwest upper birch pigs
places.note: Three adult pigs roamed between this high grassy spot and the north ridge. Dry approach from the south via Northwest birch pigs.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East workshop storage Grid
places.note: Blue Grid on the roofed cobblestone bench east of the wind machines. Use the existing workshop aisle from the Coke Oven side.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West pasture stone approach
places.note: Signed short stone path to the south double gate. Reaches the fence from the stream field without the old grassy dip.
places.author: Gary

places.name: North iron stair lower landing
places.note: Lit lower end of the original North ridge iron stair. Return south over intact stone and cobble steps. Iron remains in both walls and floor.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West stream pen workbench
places.note: Outside the pig pen by the entry sign. Moved west one block to leave the path through to the gates clear.
places.author: Gary

places.name: North ridge stray chicken
places.note: Chicken #218276 wandered this upper birch shelf at 02:40. Clear dry path from the south via the near northwest pig shelf.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Lower stream chicken coop
places.note: North entry below the wheat, signed and lit. Work one birch door at a time and look toward the hinge side to close an open door.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Pig pen south turn
places.note: From the signed field-side stairs, follow this clear ground west along the south side of the pig pen. Continue west to the bench and apron, then turn north to the gate on foot.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West stream pig pen
places.note: On the signed south approach. Walk west around the workbench, then turn north onto the stone gate landing. Use both gates one at a time and keep two adult breeders.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Pig pen west stone entry
places.note: Reach from the outside south approach via the west side of the workbench. Cobble approach with three-block two-gate passage. Leave gate openings closed when you finish.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Lower livestock trail west turn
places.note: Walk the south side of the wheat toward the coop and keep west to the pasture approach. This waypoint skirts the wheat, the old chicken yard and the drop under the field.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Coop west bank junction
places.note: Signed walking bank south of the upper wheat. Follow the dry grass east to the co-op north door approach or west over the filled dip to the pasture.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West livestock raised field edge
places.note: Use this dry strip along the wheat bank between the downhill cobble stair and the turn toward the coop or pasture.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West livestock south trail stair
places.note: The cobble stair below the hillside junction leads to the torch-lined raised field edge.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West livestock hillside junction
places.note: From the pig pen or cabin, follow the signed hillside path south to the pasture and coop.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West pig pen safe apron
places.note: Dry outside stance west of both gates. Open one at a time and verify both closed after leaving.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore south stair iron nook
places.note: Short west alcove off Margo’s south stair. Iron remains behind the west wall and in its floor. Keep the main steps clear.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore diamond stair last landing
places.note: Margo's south stair turns down into an exposed diamond seam here. Leave the seam and lower treads clear. Redstone branch begins a few steps higher.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore redstone branch mouth
places.note: From the diamond stair's south leg, turn east into the lit, level branch above the diamond face.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore redstone branch coal seam
places.note: Low coal vein in the walls and floor of the redstone branch. Keep floor support or replace it with cobble after gathering.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore redstone branch south turn
places.note: Turn south near the end of the straight lit branch. The working face is two short steps below the level hallway.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore redstone working face
places.note: Lit face at the south end of the branch, two treads down from the hall. Leave a solid floor and take ore from the east wall.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore diamond stair gravel bend
places.note: At the cobble tread turn south down Margo's diamond stair, or west and up toward the gold-stair junction. The east recess ends in stone.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore diamond stair cobble step
places.note: Use the new cobble stair below the raised cobble tread on the south leg to walk uphill.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Meadow kelp basin lower stand
places.note: Dry south rim below the bunkhouse. Refillable middle water cell, deep east kelp well and spare bucket in the chest to the east.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore copper working face
places.note: East spur from the upper stair, then south at the torch. Several exposed copper blocks remain, including the floor seam.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore copper spur mouth
places.note: Side spur heads east from the upper gold stair tread, then turns south toward copper at the torch.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore mid-stair stone face
places.note: Lit level bore north of the diamond stair. Enter at the mid-stair shelf, then turn east. Two exposed osmium blocks harvested at first wall.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore mid-stair stone spur mouth
places.note: Short north turn out of the stair from the step at y39, then turn east into the lit stone spur.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Far east ridge sheep sighting
places.note: Saw one wild sheep during the coastal trip. It had wandered out of view by the time I returned up the grass. Treat this as a sighting.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore trailhead shelter
places.note: Signed birch refuge west of gold stair, with bed, furnace, bench, supplies and a tested first-alloy machine pair. Enter from north porch and close the door.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore upper stair bauxite seam
places.note: On the gold stair tread, face south. Two Bauxite Ore blocks gave eight Sundries bauxite chunks. More behind the side opening. Keep the tread and floor intact.
places.author: Margo

places.name: South ravine zinc and slate fork
places.note: West branch from shallow ore torch. Follow the new stair west, turn north at the torch, then west again for zinc and slate. Eight osmium gathered from the two side pockets.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore kelp landing
places.note: Signed approach beside the water shelf. Four underwater bases on the south edge, below the waterline. Cut only tops visible one block below your feet and walk the grass and boards to collect.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East shore ore shelf
places.note: Natural exposed copper and zinc knobs on the grassy bay ridge east of the shelter. Shore approach passes inland of the inlet. Keep footholds under the cliff edge.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East coast white-cliff landing
places.note: Dry stone shelf under the tall white-banded sea cliff. I swam the headland and climbed here. Move to dry stone before stopping in the water.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East coast chalk shelf
places.note: A dry ledge midway up the white cliff with exposed Sundries chalk overhead. No wild cane found on the coast to here.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East coast cliff return crest
places.note: Working ascent from the shoreline below the chalk coast. From this crest turn inland along the grassy ledges toward the ore shelf.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East workshop lower terrace turn
places.note: Dry path by the Engineer's Workbench. To reach rear smelter, climb north via upper grass bend and turn west behind the workshop.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore bamboo stair coal seam
places.note: Coal and redstone line the first descent east of the redstone face. Follow existing lit steps and leave the treads solid.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Birch west descent IE bauxite face
places.note: From the entrance follow the straight lit stair west, turn south at the last torch for three steps, then west. The north face holds Immersive Engineering bauxite. Preserve the stair floor.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore bamboo cavern window
places.note: The lit narrow tunnel ends at a one-block viewing opening into a lush cavern. Three bamboo came through the window from the nearest stem. Keep the lower sill intact and harvest from the dry tunnel.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore bamboo tunnel south turn
places.note: At the torch, turn south toward the bamboo cavern window. The passage steps down one more block farther along.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Birch west descent entrance
places.note: Open birch clearing. Descend the lit steps due west; turn south at the last torch and then west. Zinc and proper Immersive Engineering bauxite below.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore bamboo patch
places.note: Two stems on the seaward shelf below the path. Harvest upper bamboo and leave the bases. Spare starter stays in the trailhead chest.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East oven south corner stand
places.note: Oven opens from south-east corner too. From ravine path approach via the southern uphill step and aim at the southeast middle-layer coke brick.
places.author: Margo

places.name: East workshop Engineer's Workbench
places.note: Actual two-block Engineer's Workbench. Components Blueprint in slot 0. Inputs 8–13, iron component output 4 and bulbs output 7. Approach from the south.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Wind cloche harvest chest
places.note: North-facing birch chest beside the working wind cloche. Approach from the upper grass bend, behind the storage bench. Take wheat and spare seeds. Leave dirt and seed in the machine.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Meadow cane and bamboo nursery
places.note: Raised dirt trough downhill from the kelp basin. Approach around its east end by the birches, keep the water borders, and harvest tops.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Meadow nursery bamboo stem
places.note: Gary's rooted bamboo on grass just south of the birch-side nursery approach. Cut the upper stem when it grows.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Meadow nursery starter chest
places.note: Birch chest on the west planting border beside the nursery sign. Shared starts when present. Leave the rooted plants in place.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore ravine stair upper turn
places.note: From the upper dirt path, turn east at the level cobble step beside the bank torch, then follow the stairs south to shore.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore ravine stair lower foot
places.note: From the shore side, walk uphill to the gully below the oak and turn north up the narrow cobble stair.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Jungle north cove canoe-free landing
places.note: Open-water approach from north, then climb in by the shallow stream. Wild cocoa and melon lie inland southwest. Bring food for the long swim.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Shore ravine oak steps
places.note: Follow the torches past the oak. Two cobble risers join the upper bank to the grass shelf. Stay on the grass side of the cave mouth.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Shore oak gully cave hazard
places.note: Below the oak stair and south of the stair-foot bench. Direct travel from shore dropped me beside a shaded cave mouth. Follow Gary's lit approach above the lip; do not plot through the gully floor.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West pasture birch traverse
places.note: Grass west of the pasture. Stay on the south side of the fence via West pasture stone approach, then round the large birch.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Meadow nursery melon stem
places.note: North rim of the nursery. Keep the adjacent west grass available for fruit. Harvest a melon and leave the stem.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West birch high sand saddle
places.note: Dry high sand on the west traverse. Approach over grass from the east. Water lies below to the southwest; look for a walkable contour.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West coast stone brow
places.note: Broad dry rock with exposed ore at the top of the west coastal descent. Follow the open ledges south in short legs.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West brow surface zinc
places.note: Exposed zinc ore in the floor of the high stone brow. Stand on the larger flat shelf and leave the walking surface intact.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West saddle north switchback
places.note: Climb north of the little oak from the sand saddle. The raised grass turn joins the west pasture birch traverse.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West coast high edge light
places.note: End of the upper coastal rock shelf. The cliff past the torch falls in large drops. Keep inland or turn uphill.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West coast inland lower birches
places.note: Dry standing point on the inland descent. Skeleton followed near the birch traverse in rain. Continue south on grass to approach the coast from above.
places.author: Margo

places.name: East workshop lower fuel furnace
places.note: Ordinary fuel furnace immediately west of the low crafting table. Use the south grass approach.
places.author: Margo

places.name: East stream cookfire
places.note: Stand on the low grass east of the furnace. Aim north at the wooden base. Four food items cook at once. Pick them up without stepping onto the hearth.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East workshop wind sawmill
places.note: Dry north-side stance. Machine is one west and one south against the vertical power bypass. Load plain logs for planks and sawdust. Keep the rear smelter aisle clear.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Birch descent lapis face
places.note: Lit dry lapis face. From lower Birch Descent take the south stair, turn east at the lowest gravel bypass torch, then south twice in the marked turns. Leave the floor and stairs intact.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Birch lapis gravel bypass
places.note: Avoid the loose bank. From the south stair go east one step, north one step, then east down the long torch-lit leg. Return by the same bends.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Birch lapis stair toe
places.note: Bottom of the long east stair. Turn south down three steps, east in the level clay bore, then south into the lapis face. Return west toward the gravel bypass.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Birch descent south branch junction
places.note: At the lower torch turn south for the lapis staircase. The short north branch holds Immersive Engineering bauxite. Return up the stone stairs to the east.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West cliff sea window
places.note: Signed, lit dry opening at the end of the west rock stair. Fill a bucket or fish from inside. The seaward lip drops into water. Use the marked turns inland.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West stone stair lower turn
places.note: Turn south from the stair into the lit sea passage. Keep level. Wait until the walk has actually settled before issuing the next turn.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West sea passage elbow
places.note: From the stair, turn west here along the level passage. Inbound from sea, turn north for the climb.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West sea window corridor
places.note: Turn south from here for the signed window. From the window, turn east for the stair.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West ocean stair entrance
places.note: Signed stone tread below the brow. Step east once, turn north at the cobble curb, then follow the enclosed lit stair east.
places.author: Gary

places.name: West brow staircase approach
places.note: From the stone brow follow the dry stone contour southwest to the shallow chute. Turn south at x0 and take the cobble step east to the signed stair. The earlier high edge is an overlook.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East workshop output chest
places.note: Signed wind pickup. Iron ingots, IE aluminum and birch saplings reach the chest above the sign. Check existing batches first and collect your own. Use lower terrace for the rear smelter.
places.author: Margo

places.name: East workshop rear smelter
places.note: Stand here and look southwest low at the Energized Smelter's east face. Wind-powered. Top RS Exporter feeds iron grit and north RS Importer collects iron and IE aluminum. Leave both in place.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Northwest birch coast overlook
places.note: New open western sea, reached on a dry contour from the north birch ridge. Drop is steep. Stay on grass or find a shallow notch before going to the water.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Northwest granite shoreline traverse
places.note: A wide bare coastal shelf reached by staying high along the shore north of the birch overlook. There are ore exposures and deep shady cracks inland. Keep to the open contour.
places.author: Margo

places.name: North coast wild cane beach
places.note: Natural sugar cane on the sea-facing shelf where gravel meets the sand. Cut the upper block and leave the rooted base. Water crossing is west of this beach.
places.author: Margo

places.name: Meadow nursery cane root
places.note: Sugar cane on the southeast grass rim beside the trough. Stand on the middle dry rim to cut an upper block. Leave the base and water in place.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West sea hearth
places.note: Dry lit alcove by the sea window corridor. The chest and bench sit beside the campfire. Use stand in front of chest; retrieve catch from clear stone. Borrow and return the local rod.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Workshop east grass bend
places.note: From the lower bench use the east grass bend, then turn west for the pickup chest or north for the cloche. Stay outside the Workshop walls.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West sea casting stone
places.note: Left side of the dry window. Aim due south, about 22 degrees down to cast. Angle the view farther down to keep the float above the crosshair. Reel on its sharp dip. Salmon and cod tested.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Meadow nursery south step
places.note: Cobble step levels the dip. From the east torch go across it, then turn north at the grass step to reach the dry middle nursery rim.
places.author: Margo

places.name: West ocean stair middle landing
places.note: Gary showed this two-tread landing. Continue east downhill to the clay shelf, or west uphill to the level cobble curb by the sign.
places.author: Margo

places.name: East stream cane root
places.note: Shared sugar cane on the north grass edge of the waterlogged birch slab. Reach from the dry strip by the cabin steps. Clip only upper growth and keep the root and slab.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Cabin berry walk turn
places.note: Follow the dry path north along the cabin’s east side. Turn east one block onto the birch slab, then north into the signed picking lane. Turn east to walk the four bushes while staying on the path.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Birch slope crafting table
places.note: Existing workbench on the flower slope. Reach from the grass step to its north. I opened it and made a shovel.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Meadow honey level crossing
places.note: Flat existing rail. Look both ways and cross straight north-south at track height. Do not dig or place on the rail. The honey ledge is two blocks south, the signed nursery route turns east three to four blocks north.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Meadow nursery honey path
places.note: From the nursery foot continue west along the dirt path. At the lit turn head south across the flat rail at track height, then two blocks to the nest ledge. Rail and nursery rims stay in place.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Honey ledge upper grass approach
places.note: Below the workshop path, walk south over the gravel and grass to the lower shelf. Reach the flat crossing from the north. Follow the marked path east to the nursery or cross straight to the nest.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East workshop pickup standing spot
places.note: Dry aisle facing the birch pickup chest above the sign. Check initial stock and allow the smelter to finish after the Enrichment Chamber clears.
places.author: Gary

places.name: East stream cane second root
places.note: Grown from the first upper cutting of the cabin stream cane. Leave the base and take upper growth.
places.author: Gary

places.name: Cabin porch berry corner
places.author: Gary
places.note: Level cobblestone turn. Walk straight east from the door landing across the two blocks, then turn north along the cabin wall.
